thread:
sam: Kicking off POC for BridgeWave to migrate from CompetitorX API. Main asks: header mapping, rate-limits, auth parity, and SCCQ. Any immediate blockers?
jordan: noted. can you paste their sample request/response?
sam: pasted below:
Customer sample:
GET /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <tokenX>
X-Customer-TTL: 30
body: {"prompt":"..."}
Response has "choices" array and "metadata.request_id"
They expect same token billing semantics as CompetitorX.
mike: quick notes: header X-Customer-TTL maps to Redwood max_tokens concept, but we don't accept a TTL header today. we can support via proxy header mapping. CompetitorX streams a single "delta" chunk per token; Redwood streams SSE with token events — should be compatible for most clients.
jordan: rate limits: they have 120 rpm per org. Redwood per-tenant rate limiter can replicate. need to confirm burst policy and 429 body shape if their middleware parses it.
sam: TODO: produce mapping doc + small proxy shim. POC scheduled Mon.
emily: SCCQ flag: they require KMS/HSM details, data retention, and egress controls. send their questionnaire.
sam: pasted SCCQ excerpt: Q1: "Do you allow raw request logs to leave region?"
emily: answer: For Dedicated/Private we support regional log retention. For hosted, logs are stored in customer region with option to disable request-body logging. engineering ack needed to confirm we can disable request body logging per-tenant.
mike: confirmable. we can flip off request-body logging per-tenant within 24h, but metrics and token-counts remain.
kate: pricing ask from customer: they expect parity with CompetitorX at $2/1k tokens. our hosted list is $3.2/1k. Presales: can we offer trial credits or short-term committed pricing for POC?
sam: propose 3-month POC credit 50k tokens + revisit committed pricing if they convert.
jordan: technical blocker: CompetitorX uses user_id session affinity header. we should mirror header (x-forwarded-session) and use sticky routing to preserve stateful KV cache. needs config change.
mike: sticky routing doable, but will add ~5% tail latency on busy workers. will quantify.
sam: they also expect exact 429/503 JSON shapes so their middleware doesn't break.
jordan: I can add a response-normalizer in the shim to rewrite errors to competitor shape. low effort.
emily: SCCQ: pen test frequency question — we run annual third-party pentests + continuous internal scans. I'll author the formal response.
sam: owners: mike (shim & logging toggle), jordan (rate-limit + response mapping), emily (SCCQ answers), kate (pricing). I'll send invite Mon 10am PT.
kate: noted. adding legal: @legal please confirm POC credit contract language.
legal-bot: @sam legal review required. please send SOW draft to legal@redwood.com with POC terms.
sam: sample shim config I'll drop in PR:
```
proxy:
  header_map:
    X-Customer-TTL: max_tokens
  rewrite_errors: true
  error_shape: competitorx_v1
```
mike: will fork runtime-proxy and open PR. ETA Wed.
sam: any other blockers?
jordan: need to validate tokenization differences — CompetitorX token counts differ. run 20-sample prompts to measure delta and document billing implications.
sam: good call. mike can run token-count batch.
mike: running this afternoon, will post results.
sam: thanks team, I'll update BridgeWave after internal sync.
